channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: .NET: BinaryFormatter serialization and deserialization have been removed
item.description: .NET 9 removed the BinaryFormatter implementation: the type still compiles, but every call throws PlatformNotSupportedException. It was deprecated because deserialising untrusted data with it allows remote code execution. Code that has not touched it directly often still hits it through an old…

item.title: .NET: NETSDK1045: The current .NET SDK does not support targeting .NET 10.0
item.description: The project's TargetFramework is newer than the SDK doing the build. Installing the new runtime is not enough, you need the matching SDK. The usual surprise is a global.json pinning an older SDK, or a CI image or Visual Studio install that lags behind, so the project builds on one machine and not…

item.title: Airflow: DAG.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'schedule_interval'
item.description: Airflow 3 removed the schedule_interval and timetable arguments that had been deprecated since 2.4; a DAG now takes a single schedule argument. Every DAG file written for Airflow 2 fails to import after the upgrade and shows up as a Broken DAG, even though nothing in the file changed. The same…

item.title: Alertmanager: Notify for alerts failed: notify retry canceled after 16 attempts
item.description: Alertmanager tried to deliver a notification until the group's retry window ran out, and every attempt failed. The line itself only says it gave up; the reason follows it, usually a webhook returning 4xx, a Slack or Teams URL that was revoked, an SMTP relay rejecting the login, or DNS and proxy…

item.title: Ansible: [WARNING]: Platform linux on host web1 is using the discovered Python
item.description: Ansible had to guess which Python to run modules with on the managed host, and warns because a later package install could change the answer. It is harmless on its own, but the same guessing is behind confusing failures elsewhere: a module that says a library is missing when you installed it for a…

item.title: Ansible: Conditionals must have a boolean result
item.description: ansible-core 2.19 rewrote templating and stopped guessing the truthiness of non-boolean values in when, until, failed_when and changed_when. A condition like when: my_var, where my_var holds the string "false" or a list, used to be coerced quietly and sometimes wrongly; now it fails the task…

item.title: Ansible: ERROR! the role 'nginx' was not found in
item.description: Ansible searched its role path and found no directory with that name. The search starts relative to the playbook file, not the directory you run the command from, so moving a playbook into a subfolder breaks roles that sat next to it. Roles from Galaxy also need installing on each machine that…

item.title: ASP.NET Core: Synchronous operations are disallowed. Call ReadAsync or set
item.description: Kestrel and IIS block synchronous reads and writes on the request and response bodies, because a blocked thread per request starves the thread pool under load. The exception usually comes from a library rather than your code: an XmlSerializer, an old Newtonsoft.Json formatter, or a…

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.HandlerNotFound: index.handler is undefined or not exported
item.description: Lambda found and loaded the file named in the handler setting, but that file has no export called handler. The usual causes are a default export instead of a named one, a build step that puts the file in dist/ while the handler setting still says index, or a TypeScript build that was never run so…

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.UserCodeSyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside
item.description: The Node.js runtime decides whether your handler is an ES module or CommonJS from the file extension and the nearest package.json, exactly as Node does locally. An index.js containing import statements is treated as CommonJS unless package.json says "type": "module". Locally a bundler or ts-node…

item.title: Azure Functions: No job functions found. Try making your job classes
item.description: The host started but indexed zero functions, so there is nothing to run. The message talks about public classes, which is a .NET in-process hint, yet the real cause is usually elsewhere: FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME not matching the code, a .NET isolated app deployed with the in-process setting, a…

item.title: Cloudflare: cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
item.description: DYNAMIC means Cloudflare never considered the response for caching, which is different from a MISS. By default Cloudflare only caches static file extensions such as .css, .js and images; HTML and API responses pass straight through however long your Cache-Control max-age is. Adding headers at the…

item.title: Django: CacheKeyWarning: Cache key will cause errors if used with memcached
item.description: Memcached keys must be under 250 bytes and contain no spaces or control characters. Django warns about this on every backend so that code developed against the local memory cache does not break when it reaches a memcached production cluster. The usual culprits are keys built from URLs, search…

item.title: Fluent Bit: Action/metadata line [1] contains an unknown parameter [_type]
item.description: Elasticsearch 8 removed mapping types, and rejects any bulk request that still sends _type. Fluent Bit's es output sent _type: _doc by default, so a pipeline that was working breaks the moment the cluster is upgraded, with every chunk failing as HTTP 400. Every chunk is rejected, so nothing…

item.title: Grafana: Datasource ${DS_PROMETHEUS} was not found
item.description: The dashboard was exported for sharing, which replaces every data source with a placeholder input like ${DS_PROMETHEUS}. The import screen normally asks you to map that input to a real data source, but provisioning, the HTTP API and Terraform skip that step and load the placeholder as if it were a…

item.title: gRPC: CANCELLED (code 1)
item.description: The call was cancelled, almost always by the caller rather than the server. In Go the client context was cancelled (often a deferred cancel() or an HTTP request that ended), in Node and Python the client closed the call or the channel. Seen on the server, it means the client gave up and any…

item.title: gRPC: UNAVAILABLE: DNS resolution failed for service
item.description: The channel could not turn the target into an address. Besides a plain typo, two gRPC quirks cause it: the target string uses its own URI syntax, so a scheme like http:// or a trailing path is read as part of the hostname, and C-core may use the c-ares resolver, which ignores /etc/hosts entries…

item.title: gRPC: UNAVAILABLE: failed to connect to all addresses
item.description: This is the C-core wording (Python, Node's older grpc package, Ruby, C++, PHP) for a channel that resolved its target but could not open a working connection to any of the addresses. The text hides the real cause, which follows it in the debug string: connection refused, a TLS mismatch, a…

item.title: Java: PatternSyntaxException: Dangling meta character '*' near index 0
item.description: A quantifier such as *, + or ? appeared with nothing before it to repeat. It almost never comes from a regex you meant to write: String.split, replaceAll and matches all take a regular expression, so splitting on "+" or "*" as a plain separator fails. The same code works with "," or ";" because…

item.title: JavaScript: Invalid regular expression: Duplicate capture group name
item.description: Reusing a named group in different alternatives, as in (?\d{4})-\d{2}|\d{2}/(?\d{4}), only became legal in ES2025. Chrome 125, Firefox 129 and Safari 17 accept it; older browsers, older Node versions and some bundler parsers throw at the moment the script loads. A pattern that passes every test on…

item.title: libvirt: Cannot access storage file (as uid:107, gid:107): Permission denied
item.description: The system libvirt daemon starts QEMU as an unprivileged user (qemu or libvirt-qemu, uid 107 on many distributions), not as you. That user needs search permission on every directory leading to the disk image, so an image in your home directory fails even when the file itself is world readable. On…

item.title: Loki: error at least one label pair is required per stream
item.description: Loki indexes streams by their labels and will not accept a push whose stream has none. The shipper is configured, but its relabelling dropped every label: commonly a Promtail or Alloy relabel rule with action keep or labeldrop matching too much, or Kubernetes discovery labels that start with __…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS50076: Due to a configuration change made by your
item.description: A Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for this sign-in, and the client used a flow that cannot show an MFA prompt: the resource owner password grant, a legacy SMTP or IMAP client, or a script calling with a username and password. Interactive sign-ins from the same…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS700016: Application with identifier was not found
item.description: The client_id in the request does not exist in the tenant the request was sent to. Usually the app is single tenant and the code points at /common or /organizations, or a user from another organisation is signing in to an app that was never made multi-tenant. Copying the object ID instead of the…

item.title: Next.js: Failed to set Next.js data cache, items over 2MB can not be cached
item.description: The App Router stores fetch() responses in its data cache, and refuses any single response over 2MB. The page still renders, but that fetch runs again on every request, so a page you expected to be static quietly hits your API each time. It usually shows up when an endpoint grows past the limit…

item.title: OAuth 2: {"error":"unsupported_grant_type"}
item.description: The token endpoint did not see a grant_type it accepts. Far more often than a genuinely unsupported grant, the parameter is there but unreadable: OAuth 2 requires the token request as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and many HTTP clients send a JSON body by default. The server finds no…

item.title: Postfix: 450 4.1.8 Sender address rejected: Domain not found
item.description: The receiving Postfix has reject_unknown_sender_domain enabled and could not find an A or MX record for the domain in your MAIL FROM address. It is a 4xx, so the sender retries and the mail sits in the queue. Common causes are an application sending from an internal name like app.local, a server…

item.title: Prometheus: opening storage failed: lock DB directory: resource temporarily
item.description: Another Prometheus process already holds the lock file in the data directory. Two Prometheus servers must never share a TSDB directory, so this check is protecting your data. It normally means an old process never exited, a second container or systemd unit points at the same volume, or a…

item.title: Python: --- Logging error --- TypeError: not all arguments converted
item.description: The logging module formats messages lazily with the % operator, and a call like logger.info("user", user_id) passes an argument with no %s to put it in. Logging deliberately does not raise: it prints this block to stderr and drops the message, so the program carries on and the log you wanted is…

item.title: sed: -e expression #1, char 15: unknown option to `s'
item.description: sed ended the s command early because the pattern or replacement contained the delimiter, nearly always a / inside a path or URL. Everything after that slash is read as flags, and the first character that is not a valid flag triggers the error. It typically appears when a shell variable is…

item.title: SMTP: 530 5.7.0 Must issue a STARTTLS command first
item.description: The server requires an encrypted session before it will accept AUTH or MAIL FROM, and the client went straight in over plain text. Usually the client is configured for port 25 or 587 with TLS switched off, or it is set to implicit TLS mode on a port that expects STARTTLS. The opposite mismatch…

item.title: SMTP: 550 5.7.25 The IP address sending this message does not have a PTR record
item.description: Gmail checks that the sending IP has reverse DNS, and that the name it points to resolves forward to the same IP. The PTR record lives with whoever owns the IP block, usually your hosting provider, not in your own DNS zone, which is why adding records to your domain changes nothing. New VPS hosts…

item.title: Spark: [CAST_INVALID_INPUT] The value 'abc' of the type "STRING" cannot be cast
item.description: Spark 4.0 turned ANSI SQL mode on by default. A cast that used to quietly return NULL for a malformed value now fails the whole query, and so do integer overflow and division by zero ([DIVIDE_BY_ZERO]). Jobs that ran for years start failing on the first dirty row after the upgrade, and the bad…

item.title: Spark: UnsupportedFileSystemException: No FileSystem for scheme "s3"
item.description: Hadoop does not ship an implementation for the plain s3:// scheme outside Amazon EMR. Open source Spark talks to S3 through the s3a:// connector in the hadoop-aws jar, which is not on the classpath of a stock Spark download. The same path works on EMR or Databricks, which bundle their own S3…

item.title: Vagrant: The IP address configured for the host-only network is not within
item.description: VirtualBox 6.1.28 started restricting host-only networks to 192.168.56.0/21 on Linux and macOS. Vagrantfiles that have used addresses like 10.0.0.10 or 192.168.33.10 for years stop working after a VirtualBox update, and Vagrant passes on the refusal. The address is fine as an address; VirtualBox…

item.title: WSL: HCS_E_HYPERV_NOT_INSTALLED
item.description: WSL 2 runs its distros in a lightweight virtual machine, and Windows could not create it. Either the Virtual Machine Platform feature is off, or hardware virtualisation (Intel VT-x, AMD SVM) is disabled in the firmware. A BIOS update or reset often turns it back off silently, which is why WSL can…

item.title: Apache: AH01071: Got error 'Primary script unknown'
item.description: The message is PHP-FPM's, relayed by Apache: the script path Apache sent over FastCGI does not exist, or cannot be read, from PHP-FPM's point of view. Usually the handler builds the path from the wrong document root, or PHP-FPM runs in a container where the code lives somewhere else. The browser…

item.title: App Store Connect: ITMS-91053: Missing API declaration
item.description: Since May 2024 Apple rejects uploads that call certain "required reason" APIs, such as UserDefaults, file timestamps or system boot time, without a privacy manifest saying why. The call is often in a third-party SDK rather than your code, so updating the dependency to a version that ships its own…

item.title: C++: error: 'format' is not a member of 'std'
item.description: std::format is C++20 and lives in , which needs both the C++20 flag and a recent enough standard library: GCC 13, Clang 17 with libc++, or Visual Studio 2019 16.10. GCC still defaults to C++17, so one build file without the flag is enough. On macOS the deployment target matters as well as the…

item.title: C++: error: 'uint8_t' does not name a type
item.description: The file uses fixed-width integer types without including , and only ever compiled because another standard header pulled it in indirectly. GCC 13 trimmed those internal includes in libstdc++, so code that built for years breaks on upgrade, often inside a third-party library. The same happens with…

item.title: C++: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
item.description: An allocation asked for more memory than the allocator could provide, nothing caught the exception, and the runtime aborted. On Linux, real memory exhaustion usually brings the OOM killer instead, so this message more often means one absurd request: a negative length converted to size_t, a size…

item.title: Dart: Bad state: No element
item.description: firstWhere, first, last or single ran on a collection with nothing in it, or nothing matching, and these throw a StateError rather than returning null. It tends to pass in testing and fail in use, because the list is only sometimes empty: an empty API response, a search with no hits, a list read…

item.title: Emscripten: RuntimeError: Aborted(). Build with -sASSERTIONS for more info.
item.description: Emscripten's runtime hit a fatal condition and called abort(), but release builds leave out assertions to save size, so the reason was thrown away. Behind the empty brackets is usually a failed allocation, a C++ exception in a build without exception support, or a call into the module before the…

item.title: ethers v6: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Web3Provider')
item.description: ethers v6 removed the providers, utils and constants namespaces, so v5 code such as ethers.providers.Web3Provider or ethers.utils.parseEther reads a property of undefined. It usually appears when a fresh npm install pulled v6 into a project or tutorial written for v5. The classes still exist…

item.title: Flutter: Looking up a deactivated widget's ancestor is unsafe
item.description: Code used a BuildContext after its widget had left the tree, almost always after an await: the user navigated away or the dialog closed, then the callback carried on and called Navigator.of(context) or ScaffoldMessenger.of(context). The context object still exists but has nowhere in the tree to…

item.title: ingress-nginx: 400 The plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port
item.description: The controller is speaking plain HTTP to a backend that only accepts HTTPS, and the backend's own web server answers with this 400. ingress-nginx proxies to pods over HTTP unless told otherwise; it does not guess TLS from a Service port of 443. Apps that terminate their own TLS, such as Argo CD or…

item.title: Ingress: spec.rules[0].http.paths[0].pathType: Required value
item.description: networking.k8s.io/v1 made pathType mandatory on every path, where the old v1beta1 API filled it in for you. Manifests and Helm charts converted by changing only the apiVersion fail validation here, and usually on the backend fields next, since those changed shape too. The choice matters: Prefix…

item.title: macOS: zsh: killed ./app (Killed: 9) on Apple silicon
item.description: On Apple silicon every arm64 executable must carry a valid code signature, even if only an ad hoc one, and the kernel kills it at launch if the signature no longer matches the file. The program is usually fine: something changed it after linking, such as install_name_tool, strip or a patch script…

item.title: MetaMask Tx Signature: User denied transaction signature (4001)
item.description: Code 4001 is the EIP-1193 "user rejected" error: the person clicked Reject or closed the wallet popup, nothing reached the chain and no gas was spent. It is a normal outcome rather than a fault, so an app that reports it as a crash, or retries it, is the bug. ethers wraps it as ACTION_REJECTED. If…

item.title: nginx: [warn] conflicting server name "example.com" on 0.0.0.0:80, ignored
item.description: Two server blocks on the same address and port both claim the same server_name, so nginx keeps the first one it read and ignores the other for that name. Because it is only a warning the reload succeeds, and the symptom is that your edits seem to have no effect. The usual cause is a leftover copy…

item.title: nginx: the "listen ... http2" directive is deprecated, use the "http2" directive
item.description: Since nginx 1.25.1, HTTP/2 is switched on with its own http2 directive rather than a parameter on listen. The old form still works for now, so this is only a warning and nginx -t passes, which makes it easy to ignore. It turns up on every reload once nginx is upgraded underneath configs copied…

item.title: PHP 8.1: Passing null to parameter #1 ($string) of type string is deprecated
item.description: Built-in functions used to treat null as an empty string or zero. PHP 8.1 deprecated that, so trim(null), strlen(null) and friends now log a deprecation, and a future major version is set to make it a TypeError. The null usually comes from a missing form field, a nullable database column or a…

item.title: PHP: count(): Argument #1 ($value) must be of type Countable|array, null given
item.description: Since PHP 8.0, count() throws a TypeError for anything that is not an array or a Countable object. PHP 7.2 only warned, and before that count(null) quietly returned 0, so code that counted a value which might be null worked for years and breaks on upgrade. The fix belongs where the null comes…

item.title: PHP: Warning: Cannot modify header information - headers already sent by
item.description: Something was written to the response before header(), setcookie() or session_start() ran, and once the first byte has gone out the headers are fixed. The message names the file and line where output started, and the output is often invisible: whitespace after a closing ?>, a UTF-8 byte order…

item.title: Rails: could not obtain a connection from the pool within 5.000 seconds
item.description: Each thread that touches the database needs its own connection, and every connection in the pool stayed checked out for longer than checkout_timeout. The cause is rarely a slow database: it is usually a pool smaller than the number of threads, such as Puma threads or Sidekiq concurrency set higher…

item.title: Ruby 3: ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 2, expected 1)
item.description: Ruby 3.0 separated keyword arguments from positional ones, so a hash passed where a method expects keywords is now counted as an extra positional argument. Code that ran on Ruby 2.7, perhaps with a deprecation warning nobody read, fails after the upgrade. The usual places are wrappers that forward…

item.title: Ruby: Psych::BadAlias: Unknown alias: default
item.description: Psych 4, the YAML library that ships with Ruby 3.1 onwards, made YAML.load safe by default, and safe loading refuses aliases such as <<: *default unless asked. Files that have always used anchors, database.yml above all, fail when an older gem or Rails version loads them with the plain call. The…

item.title: Rust: Could not find specification for target "wasm32-wasi"
item.description: Rust renamed the wasm32-wasi target to wasm32-wasip1 to make room for WASI 0.2, then removed the old name entirely in Rust 1.84. Build scripts, CI workflows and tutorials that still say wasm32-wasi fail as soon as the toolchain updates, though no code changed. The output is the same WASI preview 1…

item.title: sbt: found version conflict(s) in library dependencies
item.description: Two dependencies need different versions of the same library, sbt picked the newer one, and the version scheme that library declares says the two are not binary compatible. Since sbt 1.5 that is an error rather than a warning, because it tends to end in a NoSuchMethodError at runtime. It typically…

item.title: Scala 3: Implicit parameters should be provided with a `using` clause
item.description: From Scala 3.7 the compiler warns when you pass an argument to an implicit parameter list by plain application, as in xs.sorted(ord). Scala 3 wants the call site to say using, so a reader can tell the argument fills an implicit slot. It arrives in large numbers when an existing codebase upgrades…

item.title: Scala module 2.15.2 requires Jackson Databind version >= 2.15.0 and < 2.16.0
item.description: jackson-module-scala refuses to register unless jackson-databind on the classpath has the same minor version, and something else pulled databind up or down. In Spark jobs the usual culprit is the Jackson that Spark itself ships, which is why the job runs locally and fails once submitted to the…

item.title: Solidity: CompilerError: Stack too deep. Try compiling with --via-ir
item.description: The EVM can only reach the top 16 slots of its stack, and the function the error points at needs more than that for its locals, parameters and return values at once. The legacy code generator cannot move values to memory to make room, so it gives up. The IR pipeline can, which is why the compiler…

item.title: Svelte 5: Using `<slot>` to render parent content is deprecated
item.description: In Svelte 5, content passed into a component arrives as snippets and is rendered with {@render}; survives only for compatibility. The warning appears once a component runs in runes mode, which is why it shows up after migrating a single file. A component cannot use both styles, so convert its…

item.title: Svelte 5: Using `on:click` to listen to the click event is deprecated
item.description: Svelte 5 treats DOM event handlers as ordinary attributes, onclick={...}, so the on: directive is deprecated in runes mode, and one component cannot mix the two forms. Event modifiers such as |preventDefault went too, which means a plain search and replace is not enough. Component events change as…

item.title: SvelteKit: Error: Not found: /favicon.ico
item.description: The browser asked for /favicon.ico, no route or static file matched, and SvelteKit logged the 404 the same way it logs any error. The page itself is fine. It fills the dev server log because browsers request the icon on their own whether or not the HTML links one, and the same message with another…

item.title: The argument type 'String?' can't be assigned to the parameter type 'String'.
item.description: Under sound null safety a type ending in ? might be null, and Dart will not pass it where a non-nullable value is required until you show it is not. The value usually comes from a map lookup, a nullable field or a parsed model, all of which are nullable even when you know the data is there. Adding…

item.title: Traefik: middleware "default-redirect@kubernetescrd" does not exist
item.description: A router refers to a middleware by a name Traefik cannot find. With the Kubernetes CRD provider the full name is namespace-name@kubernetescrd, so a Middleware in another namespace, or an annotation that leaves out the namespace prefix, points at nothing. Traefik keeps running and drops only that…

item.title: WebAssembly: Refused to compile or instantiate WebAssembly module
item.description: The page's Content Security Policy blocks WebAssembly compilation. Browsers treat compiling Wasm much like eval, so a script-src without 'wasm-unsafe-eval' stops it even when the .wasm file comes from your own origin. It often appears only in production or in a browser extension, because the…

item.title: Windows: The requested operation requires elevation (error 740)
item.description: The program's manifest says it must run as administrator, and the process starting it is not elevated, so Windows refuses rather than showing a UAC prompt. That is why the same installer works when double-clicked but fails from a script, a scheduled task, a CI agent or an ordinary terminal. Being…

item.title: Windows: The RPC server is unavailable (0x800706BA)
item.description: The client could not complete a remote procedure call to the target machine. RPC first contacts the endpoint mapper on TCP 135, then switches to a dynamic high port, and a firewall that allows 135 but not the high range is the classic cause. It surfaces in WMI, remote management, domain joins and…

item.title: Windows: You can't access this shared folder (guest access blocked)
item.description: Windows 11 24H2 refuses SMB guest logons and requires SMB signing by default, so a NAS, a router USB share or an old Samba server that lets anyone in as guest stops working after the upgrade, while other PCs still connect. The share is fine; the client is refusing to talk to it without…

item.title: Xcode: No signing certificate "iOS Development" found
item.description: The project wants to sign with a development certificate whose private key is not in this Mac's keychain. The certificate may well exist in your developer account, but without its key it cannot sign anything, which is why a project that builds on a colleague's Mac or your old one fails on a new…

item.title: Ansible: 'dict object' has no attribute 'stdout'
item.description: The variable exists but does not have the key you asked for. Usually that's because the task that registered it was skipped, so all it holds is skipped and changed. Or the task ran in a loop, and then the output sits under results, one entry per item. Printing the whole variable shows which of the…

item.title: Ansible: Failed to set permissions on the temporary files Ansible needs
item.description: This happens with become_user set to an unprivileged account such as postgres. Ansible uploads the module as the SSH user, and that account then has to read it. Ansible tries setfacl first, then other methods, and refuses to make the file world readable unless you tell it to. Installing the acl…

item.title: Ansible: Timeout (12s) waiting for privilege escalation prompt
item.description: Ansible ran sudo and waited for a password prompt or a success marker that never came within the timeout. It is rarely a wrong password. More often sudo itself is slow because the host cannot resolve its own hostname, a login banner or sudo lecture is in the way, or become_method does not match…

item.title: Apollo Client: Could not find "client" in the context or passed in as an option
item.description: A useQuery or useMutation hook ran outside an ApolloProvider. When the provider clearly wraps the app, there are two copies of @apollo/client in node_modules, so the hook and the provider use different React contexts. Tests that render a component without a MockedProvider fail in the same way.

item.title: AWS SQS: The specified queue does not exist or you do not have access to it
item.description: SQS gives the same answer whether the queue is missing or you lack permission, so you cannot tell which from the message. Most often the queue exists in another region or account from the one the client is using. Or the code built a URL from the queue name instead of calling GetQueueUrl. A queue…

item.title: Azure Storage: AuthorizationPermissionMismatch
item.description: You are signed in with Entra ID, and your role lets you manage the storage account but not read its data. Owner and Contributor only cover the control plane. Blob access needs a data role such as Storage Blob Data Reader or Contributor. The portal hides this because it falls back to the account…

item.title: bash: !": event not found
item.description: In an interactive shell, an exclamation mark in double quotes triggers history expansion, and bash tried to find a previous command beginning with whatever followed it. The same line works fine in a script, where history expansion is off, which is why it puzzles people. Single quotes stop it…

item.title: bash: [: : integer expression expected
item.description: A numeric comparison such as -gt or -eq got something that is not a whole number. The text between the colons is the bad value: empty means the variable was unset or a command printed nothing. A trailing carriage return from a Windows file or a decimal like 3.5 cause the same error, since the…

item.title: bash: [: too many arguments
item.description: A variable inside single brackets was left unquoted and its value contained spaces, or a glob that matched several files. So [ was handed more words than it can parse. Because it depends on the data, the script works for months and then breaks the first time a filename or answer has a space in it.

item.title: C#: Collection was modified; enumeration operation may not execute
item.description: You added or removed items in a List or Dictionary while a foreach was still walking it, and the enumerator noticed the version change. In a single thread the fix is simple. If the loop body never touches the collection, another thread does, and taking a copy only hides a race that needs a lock or…

item.title: C#: CS0246 The type or namespace name could not be found
item.description: The compiler cannot see the type at all. It might be a missing using directive or NuGet package, but just as often the package is there and targets a different framework than the project. Or the type sits in a project that is not referenced. When the IDE is happy and dotnet build is not, a stale…

item.title: Connection to node -1 could not be established. Broker may not be available.
item.description: Node -1 is the bootstrap server, so the client could not even make its first connection. If bootstrap works and a later node fails, the broker is returning advertised.listeners that the client cannot reach, such as a container hostname or localhost. item.description: An effect wrote to state that it also reads, so running it schedules it again and Svelte gives up after a fixed number of iterations. Deriving a value inside an effect is the usual shape, and the loop often only closes once a second effect starts reading what the first one writes.

item.title: SvelteKit: Cannot access url.searchParams on a page with prerendering enabled
item.description: A prerendered page is one file written at build time, so there is no request to read a query string from. The clash usually comes from a layout: prerender was switched on once near the root and inherited by a page that filters or paginates from the URL.

item.title: SvelteKit: Cannot import $env/static/private into client-facing code
item.description: Private environment variables may only be imported by modules that never reach the browser, and the import chain from a component or a universal load function crossed that line. The offending import is often indirect: a shared helper that reads a secret gets pulled into a .svelte file by one…

item.title: SvelteKit: Cross-site POST form submissions are forbidden
item.description: SvelteKit compares the Origin header with the origin it believes it is serving and rejects the mismatch, which is its CSRF protection rather than a bug. It appears behind a proxy that does not pass the original host and protocol through, or when a form genuinely posts to another host, such as a…

item.title: The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed
item.description: The machine account password the workstation holds no longer matches the one in Active Directory, so domain logons are refused while local accounts still work. Restoring a virtual machine from a snapshot, cloning without sysprep, or leaving a machine switched off for longer than the password…

item.title: wasm-bindgen: closure invoked after being dropped
item.description: A Rust closure handed to JavaScript lives only as long as its Closure value, and letting that fall out of scope frees it while the event listener or timer still points at it. The panic therefore arrives when the callback first fires rather than where the mistake was made, which is normally a setup…

item.title: wasm-pack: crate-type must be cdylib to compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown
item.description: A Rust library defaults to the rlib crate type, which cannot be linked into a WebAssembly module, so wasm-pack stops before it ever calls the compiler. It usually means the crate was started with cargo new rather than from the wasm template, or that a new workspace member inherited the default.

item.title: Web3: could not detect network (event="noNetwork", code=NETWORK_ERROR)
item.description: ethers asks the endpoint for its chain id before it will do anything else, and that call failed, so the provider never finished starting. A wrong URL is only one cause: a missing key in the path, a rate limited key, a browser CORS rejection and an http endpoint on an https page all look identical…

item.title: Web3: max code size exceeded when deploying a contract
item.description: EIP-170 caps deployed runtime code at 24576 bytes and the deployment is rejected once the compiled contract passes it. The growth is usually incidental rather than a single large addition: long revert strings, many public functions and inlined library code all count, and building with the…

item.title: Web3: Transaction reverted without a reason string
item.description: The contract used require without a message, tripped an assert, ran out of gas inside a nested call, or the address has no code for that selector, so there is no string to decode. The tooling reports the absence rather than the cause, which is why the same call against a live node returns only a…

item.title: Web3: transaction underpriced
item.description: The node rejected the transaction before it entered the pool because the fee offered is below the minimum it will accept, which is local policy rather than a consensus rule. It differs from the replacement case: nothing is pending for that nonce, the fee is simply under this node’s floor or under…

item.title: WebAssembly: Import #0 module="env" error: module is not an object or function
item.description: The module declares imports and the importObject handed to instantiate has no property for that namespace, so the engine gives up before linking anything. It is the normal outcome of loading an Emscripten or WASI build with a bare instantiate call, because those toolchains expect their own…

item.title: Windows: A required privilege is not held by the client (0x80070522)
item.description: Creating a symbolic link needs SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege, which standard accounts do not hold, so git checkouts, npm installs and archive extractions that contain links fail with something that reads like a file permission problem. Developer Mode grants the privilege without making the whole…

item.title: Xcode: building for 'iOS-simulator', but linking in object file built for 'iOS'
item.description: A dependency in the project carries a device slice only, and the simulator build cannot link it even though both are arm64 on Apple silicon. It turns up with an old fat framework or a binary pod published before XCFrameworks existed, and excluding arm64 hides it at the cost of breaking the…

item.title: Ansible: Failed to import the required Python library (docker) on host
item.description: Modules run on the target with the interpreter Ansible discovered there, so a library installed on the control node, or into a different virtualenv, is invisible to them. The message names the interpreter it used, and that path is the part worth reading before installing anything again.

item.title: Ansible: No inventory was parsed, only implicit localhost is available
item.description: Ansible found no usable inventory, so every host pattern matches nothing and the run ends with "skipping: no hosts matched" and an exit code of zero. A file that exists but fails to parse produces the same warning as one that is missing, which is why a YAML inventory with the wrong shape looks…

item.title: Connections hang or reset with ListenOverflows increasing
item.description: The kernel finished the handshake but the application was too slow to call accept(), so the completed connection queue filled and further connections were dropped silently. Clients see a stall and then a timeout or a reset, and nothing appears in the application log because the connection never…

item.title: DMARC: dmarc=fail (p=reject) in Authentication-Results
item.description: SPF or DKIM passed on its own but neither aligned with the domain in the From header, and alignment is what DMARC checks. This is why mail sent through a third party can pass SPF against the provider domain and still be rejected as your domain.

item.title: Elixir: (DBConnection.ConnectionError) tcp recv: closed
item.description: The database closed a pooled socket that Ecto still believed was usable, so the checkout succeeded and the query died on the wire. The usual culprit is something between the application and the database with an idle timeout: a pgbouncer server_idle_timeout, an RDS proxy, or a cloud load balancer…

item.title: Elixir: (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:error, :enoent}
item.description: A pattern match assumed the happy path and the function returned the error tuple instead, so the process crashed at the assignment rather than at the failure. The value in the message is the whole answer: it names both what went wrong and which call produced it.

item.title: Elixir: protocol String.Chars not implemented for %{} of type Map
item.description: String interpolation calls to_string/1, and only a few types implement it: maps, lists, tuples and structs do not. The failure is at runtime rather than compile time, so it usually appears in an error path or a log line that only runs when something else has already gone wrong.

item.title: Go: error parsing regexp: invalid or unsupported Perl syntax: (?!
item.description: Go uses RE2, which has no backtracking and therefore no lookahead, no lookbehind and no backreferences. That is a deliberate guarantee of linear time matching rather than a missing feature, so the pattern has to be restructured instead of escaped.

item.title: gRPC: connection error: desc = transport: Error while dialing
item.description: The channel could not open a TCP or TLS connection, so the RPC fails with UNAVAILABLE and this wrapped cause. Because Dial is lazy in the Go client, the mistake surfaces on the first call rather than at construction, which makes it look like a request problem rather than a target or credentials one.

item.title: High iowait: load average climbing while the CPU sits idle
item.description: Linux counts tasks in uninterruptible sleep towards the load average, so processes blocked on a disk or an NFS mount push load into double figures on a box that is 95 per cent idle. The number sends people hunting for a CPU problem that does not exist, when the queue is in front of a device.

item.title: ingress-nginx: Service does not have any active Endpoint
item.description: The controller resolved the Ingress to a Service but the Service selects no ready Pods, so it serves the default backend and returns 404 instead of routing. The Ingress and the Service both look correct in kubectl get, because the gap is between the Service selector and the Pod labels or the…

item.title: ingress-nginx: upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)
item.description: The controller gave up waiting for the backend and returned 504 after its own timeout, which defaults to 60 seconds and is set on the controller, not on the application. A long report or an upload that works when called directly against the Service will fail through the Ingress for exactly this…

item.title: Ingress: ADDRESS column stays empty and the host never resolves
item.description: kubectl get ingress shows no address because no controller has claimed the object, so nothing ever programmes a load balancer or writes the status back. The Ingress itself is valid, which is why it is accepted without complaint and then does nothing at all.

item.title: Java: PatternSyntaxException: Illegal repetition
item.description: A brace appears where the engine expects a quantifier, so a literal { in the pattern is read as the start of {n,m} and rejected. It shows up most often when a template placeholder such as {name} is passed straight to Pattern.compile or to String.replaceAll.

item.title: libvirt: Failed to connect socket to /var/run/libvirt/libvirt-sock
item.description: virsh connected to the session daemon rather than the system one, or the user is not in the group that owns the socket. The same command works under sudo, which is the clue: it is a permission and URI problem, not a daemon that failed to start.

item.title: log4j2: ERROR StatusLogger No Log4j 2 configuration file found
item.description: Log4j 2 could not find log4j2.xml on the classpath and fell back to logging errors only to the console, which is why the application starts but INFO and DEBUG never appear. In a packaged jar the file is usually present in the source tree and missing from the artefact, not absent from the repository.
